html:
The Gandhara grave culture is a set of cemeteries in the Swat valley and nearby valleys of northern Pakistan, dated to about 1400 to 800 BCE. Archaeologists know it mainly from its graves, so the name.

The graves hold both buried bodies and cremated ashes, with pottery, bronze and iron objects. The people farmed wheat, barley and rice and kept animals in the mountain valleys. The Swat River appears as the Suvastu in the Rigveda, and many scholars connect these graves with the Indo-Aryan migrations into South Asia and the Vedic period, though the link is debated.

The region later became the heart of Gandhara.
